# @siren/board — a reusable browser board for displaying Siren diagrams

## Problem

Every browser page that embeds a Siren diagram today has to hand-roll the same chrome around
`@siren/core`'s `render()`: a real canvas-based text measurer, full-bleed responsive sizing, an
SVG scale-to-fit setup, diagnostics/error handling, and Prev/Next/Reset control wiring.
`demos/step-reveal.html` and `demos/complex-showcase.html` are proof — their `<script type="module">`
blocks are near byte-identical copies of ~80 lines of this boilerplate. Every future consumer
(docs sites, a playground, third-party embedders) would otherwise have to re-derive it from
scratch, with no single place to fix a bug in it.

## Outcome

A new `@siren/board` package ships `createBoard(container, options)`: one call mounts a
full-bleed, responsive Siren diagram with sensible defaults (real text measurement, error
display, step controls) that a consumer can override piece by piece. Both existing demo pages
are migrated onto it, deleting their hand-rolled equivalents — proving the duplication is
actually gone, not just possible to avoid.

## Scope

- New package `@siren/board`, depends on `@siren/core`.
- `createBoard(container: HTMLElement, options?: BoardOptions): Board`.
- `board.setSource(source: string)` — synchronous re-render, mirrors `render()`'s own sync contract.
- Board-default real canvas-based `TextMeasurer`, overridable via `options.measureText` (same seam
  `RenderOptions.measureText` already exposes on the core side).
- Full-bleed responsive canvas area: container fills 100%/100%, the rendered SVG scales via its
  own `viewBox` — pure CSS, no `ResizeObserver`.
- Built-in floating Prev/Next/Reset control bar, positioned relative to the board's own container
  (not the viewport, so multiple boards or a boxed/sidebar embed don't collide or fly off-page).
  On by default. `options.controls: false` disables it. `options.controls: ControlsFactory`
  replaces it with a caller-supplied one.
- Built-in error banner on fatal render failure (`svg === null`), overlaid on top of the last
  successfully rendered diagram rather than clearing it.
- `options.onDiagnostics(diagnostics)` — fired on every render/`setSource` call, fatal or not
  (includes non-fatal warnings).
- `options.onStepChange(current, total)` — fired on every step change, regardless of whether it
  was triggered by the built-in buttons or a direct `board.controller.next()/prev()/reset()` call.
- `board.controller` — read-only access to the last *successful* render's `AnimationController`.
- `board.diagnostics` — read-only diagnostics from the most recent call.
- `board.destroy()` — tears down this instance's DOM/listeners only.
- Auto-injected chrome CSS via JS, idempotent across multiple `createBoard()` calls on one page.
- Migrate `demos/step-reveal.html` and `demos/complex-showcase.html` to `@siren/board`: delete
  their hand-rolled measurer/controls/error-handling code, and once both are migrated, delete
  `demos/demo-chrome.css`'s now-obsolete `#siren-container`/`.controls` rules (page header chrome —
  `h1`/`.intro`/`.status` — is untouched, stays page-owned).

## Non-goals

- Pan/zoom or any SVG-level interaction beyond step reveal.
- Multiple diagrams / tabs inside one board instance.
- Cross-reload state persistence (step position, etc.).
- Fetching a source from a URL, or any async loading state — the consumer fetches, board only
  ever accepts an already-resolved string.
- A theme/dark-mode toggle — board never touches `data-siren-theme`; that convention stays
  entirely the consumer's own concern, unrelated to board.
- A script-tag/custom-element embed target — v1 ships as a bundler ES module only, matching
  `@siren/core`'s existing distribution model.

## Domain decisions

- **Board**: a mounted, self-contained wrapper around one `@siren/core` `render()` call, owning
  its container's DOM, its own chrome styling, and the `AnimationController` lifecycle across
  `setSource` calls. A consumer of `@siren/core`, not part of it — does not redefine or extend
  CONTEXT.md's existing "Core renderer" entry.
- A failed `setSource` does not invalidate `board.controller` — it keeps pointing at the last
  successful render's controller, matching `render()`'s own existing "don't touch the container on
  failure" behavior (`packages/core/src/index.ts`). `board.diagnostics` always reflects the latest
  call, successful or not.

## Design contract

### `@siren/board` (`createBoard`)

- **Responsibilities**: own the given container's DOM subtree; call `@siren/core`'s `render()` and
  manage the `AnimationController` reference across repeated `setSource` calls; apply full-bleed
  responsive chrome CSS (auto-injected, idempotent); render/report diagnostics; render a default
  step-control UI or delegate to a caller-supplied one; notify on step changes.
- **Non-responsibilities**: fetching or resolving a source; parsing/layout/rendering internals
  (delegated entirely to `@siren/core`); theming/dark-mode; anything to do with more than one
  diagram per instance.
- **Interface**:
  ```ts
  function createBoard(container: HTMLElement, options?: BoardOptions): Board;

  interface BoardOptions {
    source?: string;
    measureText?: TextMeasurer;             // same seam as core's RenderOptions
    controls?: boolean | ControlsFactory;    // default true; false = none; function = custom
    onDiagnostics?: (diagnostics: Diagnostic[]) => void;
    onStepChange?: (current: number, total: number) => void;
  }

  type ControlsFactory = (board: Board) => { element: HTMLElement; destroy?(): void };

  interface Board {
    readonly controller: AnimationController | null;
    readonly diagnostics: Diagnostic[];
    setSource(source: string): void;
    destroy(): void;
  }
  ```
  - Errors: none thrown for malformed Siren source — failures surface as diagnostics/the error
    banner, matching core's existing "diagnostics, never throw" convention (CONTEXT.md's
    Diagnostic entry). Passing a non-`HTMLElement` `container` is a programmer error and may throw.
  - Invariants: `controller` is `null` only until the first successful render ever happens; once
    non-null it never reverts to `null` on a later failed `setSource`. `diagnostics` always
    reflects the most recent `setSource`/construction call. Calling `destroy()` twice is a no-op.
    The injected stylesheet is appended at most once per page regardless of instance count.
  - Side effects: mutates `container`'s children; appends a `<style>` element to `document.head`
    on first use, process-wide; attaches DOM event listeners for the control bar (removed on
    `destroy()`).
- **Seam**: `measureText` (text-measurement adapter — board adds a canvas-based default alongside
  core's existing jsdom-safe one), `controls` (full UI replacement or opt-out), documented CSS
  class names on the injected DOM (light restyling without JS).
- **Dependencies**: `@siren/core` — in-process, real, not substituted (board is a thin browser
  shell around it). `TextMeasurer` — substitutable; board's own tests inject a fake instead of
  relying on jsdom's incomplete canvas support. DOM/`document` — real under jsdom for structural
  assertions; real visual/layout confirmation is a manual screenshot check, not part of the
  automated suite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `createBoard(container, { source })` mounts a rendered Siren diagram filling `container`
      edge-to-edge, scaling on container resize via CSS alone.
- [ ] `board.setSource(newSource)` re-renders synchronously; a parse/build failure leaves the
      previous diagram visible, shows an error banner, and still calls `onDiagnostics`.
- [ ] Built-in Prev/Next/Reset control bar is visible by default, positioned relative to the
      board's own container, and drives `board.controller`.
- [ ] `options.controls: false` renders no control bar; `options.controls: <factory>` renders the
      factory's element instead.
- [ ] `onStepChange` fires on every step change from either the built-in buttons or a direct
      `board.controller.next()/prev()/reset()` call.
- [ ] Creating two boards on one page injects the shared stylesheet exactly once.
- [ ] `board.destroy()` removes this instance's DOM and listeners, leaves other board instances
      and the shared stylesheet untouched.
- [ ] `demos/step-reveal.html` and `demos/complex-showcase.html` render and behave identically to
      today (visually verified), now via `@siren/board`, with their hand-rolled
      measurer/controls/error code deleted.

## Test strategy

- Seam: `createBoard`/`Board` (public interface) — integration-level tests under jsdom, injecting
  a fake `measureText` per test.
- Test type: mostly integration (through `createBoard`, asserting DOM/controller/callback
  behavior), a few narrow unit tests for the style-injection idempotency guard.
- Dependency handling: `@siren/core` used for real (no mocking — it's the thing board wraps). No
  canvas polyfill; the real canvas `TextMeasurer` is exercised only by manual/visual verification
  (demo screenshots), not by the automated suite.

## Verification

- Focused: `pnpm --filter @siren/board test -- <file>`
- Suite: `pnpm -r test`
- Static: `pnpm --filter @siren/board exec tsc --noEmit`
- Demo tickets additionally require: `pnpm --filter @siren/core build && pnpm --filter @siren/board build`,
  then serve the repo root over http(s) (e.g. `python3 -m http.server`) and visually verify both
  demo pages, per the existing convention documented in `demos/step-reveal.html`.

## Baseline

Measured at 2026-09-03, commit `f26682b`.

- `pnpm -r test`: 65/65 passing (only `packages/core` exists so far).
- `packages/core`: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean.

## Risks and deferred questions

- No general pub/sub for controller state — only the single `onStepChange` callback. A custom
  `ControlsFactory` that needs to react to *externally* triggered step changes (not its own button
  clicks) has no hook for that in v1. Deferred; revisit if a real custom-controls use case needs it.
- Script-tag/custom-element embed target (ADR-0003's "embed everywhere" ambition) is explicitly
  deferred past v1.
- Exact package name (`@siren/board`) is a proposal, not locked — cheap to rename before
  publishing since it's `"private": true` like `@siren/core` currently is.
